recipes.name: Spicy Vegan Potato Curry
ingredients_raw: 1 (1 inch) piece fresh ginger root, peeled and minced
1 (15 ounce) can garbanzo beans (chickpeas), rinsed and drained

steps.text: Place potatoes into a large pot and cover with salted water. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until just tender, about 15 minutes. Drain and allow to steam dry for 1 to 2 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir onion and garlic in hot oil until onion has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes. Season with curry powder, garam masala, cumin, salt, ginger, and cayenne pepper; cook and stir for 2 minutes more.
Add cooked potatoes, garbanzo beans, peas, and tomatoes, then pour in coconut milk. Bring to a simmer and continue cooking for 5 to 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Vegan Potato Curry
raw_recipe.description: This vegan potato curry with garbanzo beans, peas, and tomatoes in coconut milk is seasoned with aromatic spices like garam masala, cumin, and cayenne.

review.reviewBody:
I made this recipe EXACTLY as stated, and it came out so much better than I imagined it would! I thought it would be cheap and cheerful, and useful as a side to something, but it is absolutely delicious! The combination of spices is completely spot on, giving a very rich and authentic flavour, with a good amount of spicyness, but not enough to hurt! Of course it tastes better the next day, as any curry does.

The only things I would change in this recipe when I next make it (As I definitely shall), is that I will increase the amount of potatoes by at least 50%, to six or seven potatoes, and use only an 8oz can of chickpeas. The curry as it is, is more like a chickpea curry with potatoes, but I'd like potatoes to be the main feature. I think this curry would be very good too with spinach in it, instead of the peas, although its great as it is! 

ps. Im neither vegan nor vegetarian.

Very good starting point! I made it as written except I went a little easy on the cayenne and I added ~1.25 lbs diced chicken breast. I salted and peppered the chicken rather than adding salt later and I think it's plenty salty. I wouldn't add salt if you are salting the potatoes. I used 4 yukon gold potatoes, which wound up at just over 1 lb; I think this is about right. If I were to make this again, I'd cap the curry powder and garam masala at 2-3 tsp; it's good as is, but if your spices are fresh, it overwhelms the other flavors.

This is one of my first ever vegan dinner recipes, and it was great! Made as written, except with cannelloni beans instead of chickpeas (I have an allergy) and with about half the cayenne (which was plenty). The taste ended up a little bland, so I added about 1TBS more salt to taste and a squeeze of lemon juice. 

I normally don't love peas, but they were perfect in this! Added a nice little burst of sweetness. Next time I'd steam and add carrots, too, since I imagine they'd have a similar effect. Sweet potatoes would also be great.

I think next time I would omit the diced tomatoes and instead do tomato puree - the chunks were too big and bites with tomato only tasted like tomato. I'd also add heavy cream and more lemon or lime juice for flavor.

This recipe proved to be a hit with my family. I was a bit concerned with the amount of spices listed, however the dish was delicious when prepared as written. Milder palettes may require a bit less cayenne. 15 minutes may be a bit too long to boil your potato cubes if they are cut small or are less than fresh, so check tenderness at ten minutes to prevent mushiness. I threw in some cauliflower crowns into the boil during the last few minutes to add to the dish.

This was my first attempt making anything with curry, so I toned down the spices a bit, glad I did and it was DELICIOUS! I had many red potatoes on hand so I used them instead with the peeling on. I only used 3 tsp, curry & garam masala and 1 tsp cayenne it was spicy enough for us. Based on previous reviews, I used more potatoes and less garbanzos. I also used frozen peas instead of canned and only 1/2 as much as what the recipe called for. It was perfect for my family. Served over yellow rice. I will definitely make this again and tone down the spice even a little more.
Yummy!! I love this recipe! Easy preparation. for me it was a little bit too heated. I cut the cayenne pepper down by 1/4 teaspoon.

Easy, fast and really good Indian dish. I made a few changes: I mixed sweet and white potatoes, added double the amount of chickpeas and diced tomatoes (I used the large cans), used fresh peas and added them at the very last minute so they stayed firm and bright green, and only used 1/2 of the cayenne pepper.

This was s a hubby favorite now. I have done it with cayenne and without and both great. I also make it in the crockpot (low for about 8-10 hours) and it is great to come home to or for lunch the next day.
I used 1/2t cayenne and halved the rest of the spices and it was perfect for us. Added chard, no peas, 3 potatoes. Served with cilantro raita and cranberry chutney, rice and naan. Yum.

A great curry with minimal ingredients and low cost! I put cilantro on top and it really added to it! I did not put in the masala and used chopped cauliflower instead of peas. And did 2 tsp of curry powder instead of 4. Delicious!

Good flavorful recipe that in regular rotation on our family menu. To simplify, I do not peel the potatoes, nor do I pre-cook them. I just add the cubed raw potatoes in step 3, cover and cook until soft (smaller cubes means faster cooking). I also substitute a can of green beans instead of peas, but that's the only ingredient I change.
This is perfection in a pot! Super fast and easy, flexible, and truly delicious. I didn’t change a thing. Big yum from all 8 New Year dinner guests! Thanks to Megan Lee!

The first time I followed this recipe exactly. My family felt it way too spicy. Second time I did a little more of each spice except the Cayanne (only a dash) and added small chopped when I sauted the onions. So good!

This dish smells so good. I will make this again. I used 1 tsp salt, 3/4 tsp cayenne (I love spicy, but I was having company, so toned it down a little), and red onion (I didn't have a yellow onion). I'll try frozen peas and carrots for color next time. Easy and delicious. Still spicy, even with half the amount of cayenne. Yum!
I used fresh tomatoes and added 1/2 vegetable broth.
I’ve been making this curry for years - it’s the best vegan curry recipe I’ve found. Spice ratio is perfect. Great served with coconut yoghurt for a healthy dinner.

The picture is a bit deceiving as it seems to have carrot and cauliflower but went ahead anyway. Added a few finger chilli's to give more heat but I like spicey. Worked out really tasty and did add coriander at the last minute
The first time I made this I accidentally used 4 tsp of cayenne! Omg hot. Now I'm more careful when I follow the recipe and tend to just use 1/2 tsp and it's still plenty spicy for me. Delish!
